novel_features.name: Macro-constrained meal planner
novel_features.description: Auto-build a set of meals that collectively hit your protein, calorie, budget, and diet targets — offline, in one command.
novel_features.rationale: Requires arithmetic selection (greedy/knapsack) over the whole locally-mirrored menu with per-meal macros and prices; the web app shows meals one card at a time and can't compose a target-fitting set.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this when the user wants a week's worth of meals meeting nutrition or budget constraints instead of hand-picking dishes.

novel_features.name: Week-over-week menu drift
novel_features.description: See exactly which meals were added, removed, or repriced between two weekly menus.
novel_features.rationale: Requires two locally-stored weekly snapshots keyed by meal id; CookUnity keeps no menu history and the menu rotates weekly.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to track what changed on the new menu without re-scanning 300+ dishes by hand.

novel_features.name: Best-value leaderboard
novel_features.description: Rank meals by nutritional value per dollar (protein-per-dollar, calories-per-dollar) computed from the local mirror.
novel_features.rationale: Combines per-meal macros with per-box-size pricing into a ratio the site never surfaces.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Pick this when the user cares about maximizing protein or calories per dollar across the menu.

novel_features.name: Favorites on this week's menu
novel_features.description: Show which of your favorited meals are actually on the current week's menu.
novel_features.rationale: A local query over the synced isFavorite flag intersected with the current menu; the web app makes you scroll to find them.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this first after a menu drop to see if the user's liked meals are back.

novel_features.name: Meal comparison
novel_features.description: Side-by-side macro, price, chef, and allergen comparison of two or more meals.
novel_features.rationale: A local join over selected meal rows with service-specific columns; no web equivalent.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this to decide between specific candidate meals the user already has in mind.

novel_features.name: Chef roster analytics
novel_features.description: Leaderboard of chefs by dish count, average rating, average price, and cuisines on the current menu.
novel_features.rationale: Local aggregation of the chef entity embedded in every meal card; the web app has no chef analytics.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to explore the menu by chef or find highly-rated chefs.

narrative.headline: Mirror CookUnity's full weekly menu into a local database so you can plan meals offline — filter by macros, diet, and budget, and diff the menu week over week, none of which the web app can do.
narrative.value_prop: CookUnity's chef-driven menu is only visible logged-in and online, paginated across hundreds of lazy-loaded cards, with shallow filters that reset on reload. This CLI syncs the entire menu — every meal's macros, chef, price, diet tags, allergens, and ratings — into a local SQLite store, then lets you query it offline: build a macro-constrained meal plan with `plan`, rank best value with `value`, see what changed with `drift`, and search everything with FTS. Every command speaks `--json` for agents.
narrative.auth_narrative: CookUnity has no public API. Auth is the Auth0 access token your logged-in browser session already holds. Copy it from the browser (DevTools → Network → any subscription.cookunity.com request → the `authorization` header value, which is the raw token with no `Bearer ` prefix) and set `COOKUNITY_TOKEN`. The token lasts about 24 hours; re-copy it when `doctor` reports it expired.

quickstart.comment: check config and token before syncing
mirror the full menu for a delivery date into the local store (omit --param to use the next delivery date)
browse the menu offline with macro filters
auto-build a week of meals hitting your targets
rank the menu by protein per dollar

troubleshoots.symptom: doctor reports the token is missing or expired (401)
troubleshoots.fix: Re-copy the raw `authorization` header value from a logged-in subscription.cookunity.com request and set COOKUNITY_TOKEN; tokens last ~24h.
Confirm the date passed via --param date=YYYY-MM-DD is a valid upcoming delivery date (menus publish ~2 weeks ahead) and that COOKUNITY_TOKEN is set.
Run `cookunity-pp-cli sync` first; the meals command reads the local mirror.

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI when you want CookUnity's menu as data: to plan meals against macro/diet/budget constraints offline, to compare or rank meals by nutrition and value, to search the menu, or to track how the menu changes week over week. It is ideal for macro-tracking eaters, allergy-constrained households, and anyone who wants to script or feed the menu to an agent.
anti_triggers: Do not use this CLI to place, modify, or cancel a CookUnity order — it is read-only over the menu and account.
Do not use it to manage billing, subscription plan changes, or delivery addresses.
Do not use it as a general recipe database; it only covers CookUnity's current prepared-meal menu.
